recipes.name: Best Cranberry Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) can whole berry cranberry sauce

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Place onion and butter in a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Bake in the preheated oven, stirring occasionally, until onion is translucent, about 15 minutes. Remove from the oven, push onion to one side, and arrange chicken thighs in the dish in a single layer. Return to the oven and bake for 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, stir together cranberry sauce, ketchup, brown sugar, vinegar, and mustard powder in a bowl.
Remove the baking dish from the oven. Transfer cooked onions to cranberry mixture and stir until incorporated. Spoon over chicken thighs and return the baking dish to the oven.

Bake until cranberry mixture is slightly caramelized and chicken is cooked through, about 20 more minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of each thigh near the bone should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Best Cranberry Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Juicy cranberry chicken thighs bake under a sweet and tangy coating of whole cranberry sauce flavored with apple cider vinegar and mustard.

review.reviewBody: My whole family gave this a thumbs up. I used all the same ingredients, but changed the methods. Using bone-in thighs, I removed the skin, trimmed the fat, and seasoned it with garlic salt and pepper. Then, I just mixed all the other ingredients (minus butter because I didn't cook the onions beforehand) and poured it over the top and baked it at 360 for about an hour (just until the internal temperature reached 170). Cranberries were WONDERFUL in this, and the meat was so tender and flavorful just like it was slow-cooked. went with steamed rice. DELISH! Update: passed this recipe on to my friend who is a beginner cook and she said "it was a hit" with her family. Thanks again for posting this. I now keep whole cranberry sauce as a "regular" stock item in my pantry!

The prep for this recipe is far too complicated. You can cook the entire dish on the stove top in one pot, no baking. First, prepare the cranberry sauce and set it aside. Next, sautee the onion in some olive oil and butter. Since I use chicken tenderloins, I cut them into about 1.5 inch pieces and sautee them with the onion. After sauteeing the onion and chicken, add the cranberry mixture and allow it to simmer. I usually allow mine to simmer for about an hour, so by that time, the chicken is fork tender. If you love cranberries, you can also toss in a handful of dried cranberries. They will plump up when simmered in the sauce. No muss, no fuss, no baking----all done in one pot.

Too sweet! \The second time I made it, I used tomato paste, 1/4C brown sugar, and fresh cranberries. I threw all the ingredients in the food processor and spread it over the chicken, and it was much better. The next time I might try roasting baby carrots in the baking dish along with the onions.

We loved this, and the sauce is yummy. I sauteed the onion and butter in a frypan then tossed the rest of the sauce ingredients in-put the boneless, skinless thighs in the oven for 20 min. took them out covered with the sauce and cooked uncovered 25 min. longer. Oven was set at 350 (I over-looked the 400 called for in the recipe)and there was a lot of juice so I upped the temp to 400 and baked 10 min more- when I took the pan out the sauce thickened up, so maybe I shouln't have added the extra 10 mins. Most cranberry sauce in a can is 11 oz. which I used. I have tried recipes that call for dry onion soup mix; but we really liked the fresh onions in this as is less salty and fresher tasting. Goes good with cooked rice.

Made as shown, except one change in directions. We saute the onion on the stovetop and add it to the cranberry mixture. Also, part of the cranberry mixture can be reserved to add later based on personal preference.
Pretty good. Made mine with chicken breasts cut up into manageable strips, and I had to substitute ketchup with BBQ sauce since our ketchup expired last independence day. Still, turned out amazing.
I used chicken tenders and ended up using a 14oz can of cranberry sauce. My entire family - including young children like it.

This recipe was given to me 42 years ago by my mother in law. I use chicken breasts (slice them smaller so each person can have one) sauted then removed to a baking pan. Sauce is made by combining/ cooking all ingredients and pouring over and baking until done. Serve with rice, green veggie and salad. 
Yum! Great for Christmas. Can easily double for party.

I used this recipe to take for meal trains. It makes enough for a larger group or a couple days. I sometimes make it with boneless/skinless. My husband loves it too and is always happy when I make a meal train meal because I make the same meal for us. My grands love it too. A couple times when I was out of ketschup I used seafood sauce. A bit more tang because of the horseradish.

Love this recipe. It's sweet and tangy and easy to prepare. On weeknights I prepare it the night before and keep the final 20 minutes of cooking for when I get home from work. I've also put the sauce on the raw chicken and cooked it for 45 minutes straight. Comes out great either way.

I read the submitter's review and used red wine vinegar instead of apple cider vinegar and used boneless skinless chicken breasts rather than the thighs. I followed the instructions for cooking the chicken except I adjusted the time. I cooked it about 20 minutes, then drained the juice, then topped it with the sauce, and cooked another 20-30 minutes. My husband and I loved this. I served it with rice and baby lima beans.
I love this recipe I make it 3 times a month for the family. I made the recipe with the Catalina salad dressing. I didn’t like it as well as yours. This is the only one I will use
I liked how easy and flavorful this was. I used boneless skinless chicken thighs. Turned out delicious.
Was very skeptical of this recipe buy glad I made it. I used the jellied cranberries instead of the whole and it was great! The whole family enjoyed it with homemade Mac n cheese

I'm a big fan of cranberries and at first I thought twice about trying this only because my kids aren't. Then I thought, why not, I was tired of the same old baked salt & pepper chicken I usually make. To my surprise, the kiddos LOVED it.... never told them what kind of sauce it was but they didn't care because they even asked for seconds :) Thanks for this recipe, oh ya, I did use it on baked drumsticks and thighs, yummy!!!! :)
I really liked the sauce, but wasn't all that crazy about it on the chicken. Weird, I know. :) I wonder how good this would be mixed with cream cheese as a spread. Hmmm ... I wonder ... :)
We found this to be enjoyable, but seemed to be lacking a bit and tanginess.
PS: If you are using a glass baking dish, 400 degrees F is too hot; reduce the oven temperature to 375 degrees F.
